original_value: The paper presents construction and laboratory tests, as well as the first field application of a new fiber-optic rotational seismograph. The system is based on a fiber-optic gyroscope (FOG), with determined Angle Random Walk of the order of 10−8 rad/Sqrt(s) and a few rad/s maximum detectable amplitude of rotation in the frequency range from direct current (DC) to 328.12 Hz. It has been designed for the rotational seismology area of interest. This work also presents exemplary relevant measurements, which were conducted using a set of two devices installed in the geophysical observatory in Książ, Poland.

result.paraphrase: The paper describes the construction and laboratory testing of a new fiber-optic rotational seismograph, along with its first field deployment. Based on a fiber-optic gyroscope (FOG), the system has an Angle Random Walk on the order of 10−8 rad/Sqrt(s) and a maximum detectable rotational amplitude of a few rad/s over the frequency range from direct current (DC) to 328.12 Hz. It was developed for applications in rotational seismology. The work also includes sample relevant measurements taken with two devices installed at the geophysical observatory in Książ, Poland.
